mug_felix: My assumption that the mug follows a static path or predictable time-based cycle is incorrect. On day 13, it was at kitchen_table_k1 at 08:26, moved to desk_b1 by 15:10, and was previously at sink_k1 (my wrong guess). The mug moves frequently and unpredictably between kitchen, bedroom, and living room spots. Do not assume a fixed location based on time of day. Always prioritize the most recent confirmed location from the latest patrol or feedback. If no recent data exists, check the most recently visited room by Felix, but be prepared for the item to be in any of the common spots (kitchen_table_k1, desk_b1, coffee_table_l1, sink_k1).

glasses_felix: Previous note to check coffee_table_l1 for late-night queries was incorrect. On day 13 at 22:45, the item was at bed_b1, not the coffee table. It does not stay in the living room at night. Check bed_b1 for late-night queries. Morning location (bathroom_shelf_ba1) remains unconfirmed for today but was correct previously; verify with latest data.

tablet_felix: Previous note to check nightstand_b1 for late-night queries was incorrect. On day 13 at 22:51, the item was at bed_b1, not the nightstand. It does not remain on the nightstand at night. Check bed_b1 for late-night queries.

General Note: Felix’s items do not follow static daily cycles. The mug is highly volatile, moving between at least three different spots in a single day. Glasses and tablet have shifted their late-night locations to bed_b1, contradicting previous patterns of coffee_table_l1 and nightstand_b1 respectively. Always prioritize the most recent confirmed location over assumed patterns, especially for the mug. For late-night queries on day 13, bed_b1 is the confirmed location for both glasses and tablet.
